I've read both pricing pages and have enough to answer.

**Vercel gives more bandwidth on its free tier.**

| | Free tier bandwidth |
|---|---|
| **Vercel (Hobby)** | 100 GB/month of Fast Data Transfer, plus 1M CDN requests/month |
| **Netlify (Free)** | No fixed bandwidth allowance. You get 300 credits/month, and bandwidth costs 20 credits per GB. |

- **Netlify's ceiling:** if every credit went to bandwidth, 300 credits would cover about 15 GB/month. In practice it's less. The same credits also pay for production deploys (15 credits each), compute and web requests.
- **Ratio:** Vercel's free tier allows at least 6–7 times more bandwidth than Netlify's.
- **Overages:** Vercel says Hobby accounts are limited to the usage caps and can't buy extra usage. On Netlify, auto-recharge for extra credits is off by default, and the Free column in the add-on credits row is blank, so I couldn't confirm Free accounts can buy more.
- **Vercel's terms:** Hobby is for personal, non-commercial use only.

I took the 100 GB figure as the Hobby column because it's the first value in the Fast Data Transfer row. The scraped text doesn't label the columns explicitly.

As of today (2026-10-20), the current LTS is **Node.js 24 ("Krypton")**. Per the official Node.js release schedule, it stops getting security updates on **2028-04-30**.

- **Node 24:** It became LTS on 2025-10-28. Today, 2026-10-20, it moves from Active LTS to Maintenance, which means only critical bug fixes and security updates from here on.
- **Node 22 ("Jod"):** It is in Maintenance and reaches end of life on 2027-04-30.
- **Node 26:** It is due to enter LTS on 2026-10-28, eight days from now. Once it does, it becomes the current LTS. Its end of life is 2029-04-30.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/Release/main/schedule.json
